title: Latency stats with LongAdder and LongAccumulator

blocks.text: The page keeps a running maximum without locks with a `LongAccumulator` built from `Long::max` and the identity `Long.MIN_VALUE`, and counts under heavy contention with a `LongAdder`, which spreads contending threads over several cells.

items: `record(latency)` counts one value and folds it into the maximum;
`count()` returns how many values were recorded;
`max()` returns the largest value recorded, or `Long.MIN_VALUE` when none was;

blocks.text: Many threads call `record` at once, so both statistics must be atomic.

cases.says: It counts every recorded latency and keeps the largest, also when many threads record at once.
When every recorded value is negative, the maximum is the largest of them, not a made-up zero.
Before anything is recorded the count is 0 and the maximum is Long.MIN_VALUE.
reset clears both the count and the maximum.

concepts: LongAccumulator keeps an atomic maximum from Long::max and Long.MIN_VALUE, and LongAdder counts under contention.
